C.domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Create common denominator
skills.definition: Find a least common denominator and rewrite fractional parts as equivalent fractions with matching denominators before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution explicitly finds an LCD/LCM/common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are converted to equivalent fractions so the denominators match before subtracting.
Tag for mixed-number items if only the fractional parts need denominator alignment.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no equivalent-fraction conversion is performed.
Do not tag for rewriting a whole number as a mixed number with 0 fractional part unless a denominator is being matched through equivalent-fraction conversion.
Do not tag for simplification after subtraction.

skills.name: Rewrite operand form
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or nonstandard mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as adding a zero-fraction part or normalizing an improper fractional part.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus a fraction with denominator matching the other term, such as 2 = 2 + 0/8 or 3 = 3 + 0/5.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fraction part is normalized, such as 2 3/2 = 3 1/2.
Tag when a mixed number is explicitly decomposed into whole and fractional parts to enable separate subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping during subtraction; that is a later operation.
Do not tag for finding a common denominator between two nonmatching fractions unless the step is specifically rewriting operand form.
Do not tag when the solver directly subtracts same-denominator fractions without any rewriting.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator and/or subtract whole and fractional parts separately once the operands are in compatible form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a shared denominator.
Tag when whole parts and fraction parts of mixed numbers are subtracted separately without regrouping.
Tag when subtraction is performed after common-denominator conversion or operand rewriting.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for the preparatory step of creating a common denominator.
Do not tag for borrowing one whole into fractional units when the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative.
Do not tag for reducing the final answer to lowest terms.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify result
skills.definition: When needed, borrow one whole into fractional units to complete the subtraction, then express the final result in lowest terms or integer/mixed-number form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution borrows or regroups 1 whole as denominator/denominator to fix a negative fractional part.
Tag when the solution simplifies a fraction such as 2/10 to 1/5 or 9/12 to 3/4.
Tag when a zero fraction is reduced to 0 or when the final answer is combined into integer or mixed-number form after regrouping/simplification.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for ordinary subtraction that does not require borrowing and does not include simplification.
Do not tag for merely finding a common denominator.
Do not tag for initial rewriting of operands before subtraction.

A.domain: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers, including common denominators, unlike denominators, borrowing, normalization, and simplification

skills.name: Align fractional forms
skills.definition: Rewrite quantities so the fractional parts are in a compatible form for subtraction, such as finding a common denominator, expressing a whole number with a fractional part, or normalizing a mixed number with an improper fractional part.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step finds an LCD or converts fractions to equivalent fractions with a common denominator.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/n or as a mixed form like 1 + 3/3 to support subtraction.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is normalized to an equivalent standard mixed number before subtracting.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for direct subtraction when the quantities are already in compatible form and no rewriting is performed.
Do not tag for borrowing after subtraction has produced a negative fractional part.
Do not tag for final simplification or combining whole and fractional parts into the answer.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once forms are compatible, either by subtracting numerators of like fractions or by subtracting whole parts and fractional parts separately.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted for fractions with the same denominator.
Tag when whole-number parts are subtracted in a mixed-number or whole-number subtraction.
Tag when fractional parts are subtracted after denominators have been aligned or are already equal.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for finding an LCD, converting equivalent fractions, or rewriting whole/mixed numbers into compatible forms.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping to fix a negative fractional result.
Do not tag for reducing a fraction or expressing the final result in mixed-number or integer form.

skills.name: Borrow across parts
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units to continue subtraction when the fractional part of the minuend is smaller than the fractional part of the subtrahend.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly borrows 1 from the whole part.
Tag when the borrowed whole is converted into n/n and added to the fractional part before subtracting.
Tag when regrouping resolves a negative fractional intermediate result in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when subtraction is completed without any regrouping.
Do not tag for initial rewriting of a whole number as 0/n unless that step is part of the setup rather than the borrow itself.
Do not tag for simplification after the regrouped subtraction is finished.

skills.name: Simplify and compose
skills.definition: Reduce the numerical result to lowest terms and express it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, integer, or zero by combining whole and fractional parts.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is simplified to lowest terms.
Tag when whole and fractional results are combined into a mixed number or integer.
Tag when a zero fractional result is converted to 0 or when a mixed-number result is expressed in final canonical form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for denominator alignment or equivalent-fraction conversion.
Do not tag for the subtraction computation itself.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping before the final result is formed.

B.domain: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers, including unlike denominators, regrouping, normalization, and simplification

skills.name: Make common fractions
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite fractional parts as equivalent fractions before subtraction when denominators do not already match.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD or common denominator.
Tag when a step converts one or both fractions to equivalent fractions with the same denominator.
Tag for mixed-number problems if only the fractional parts are rewritten to a common denominator.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no conversion is performed.
Do not tag simple rewriting of a whole number as a mixed number with 0 over a denominator unless it is part of creating matching fractional units.
Do not tag normalization of an improper mixed number such as 2 3/2 to 3 1/2 unless a common denominator is also being created.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with a shared denominator and/or subtract the whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers once the parts are aligned.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a common denominator.
Tag when whole parts of mixed numbers are subtracted.
Tag when fraction parts of mixed numbers are subtracted after denominators already match.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as having a zero fractional part and then whole and fraction parts are subtracted.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is finding a common denominator or converting equivalent fractions.
Do not tag regrouping or borrowing steps used because the fractional subtraction would be negative.
Do not tag final simplification or recombination unless actual subtraction occurs in that step.

skills.name: Regroup or normalize
skills.definition: Rewrite a quantity by normalizing an improper mixed number or by borrowing/regrouping one whole into fractional units so subtraction can proceed correctly.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when an improper mixed number is normalized, such as 2 3/2 becoming 3 1/2.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as 1 less whole plus a full fractional unit, such as 2 becoming 1 + 3/3.
Tag when a mixed-number subtraction borrows 1 whole and converts it to denominator-over-denominator fractional units.
Tag when regrouping is used because the fractional part of the minuend is smaller than the fractional part of the subtrahend.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary subtraction of already usable whole and fraction parts when no regrouping or normalization occurs.
Do not tag finding a common denominator by itself.
Do not tag simplification of the final answer.

skills.name: Simplify and express
skills.definition: Reduce the result to lowest terms and express it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is simplified, such as 2/10 to 1/5 or 9/12 to 3/4.
Tag when 0 over a denominator is rewritten as 0.
Tag when whole and fractional results are combined into a mixed number or integer final answer.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag subtraction steps that only compute the difference.
Do not tag regrouping or normalization steps before the final result is formed.
Do not tag equivalent-fraction conversion done to create common denominators.
